beschreibung: Edge catalog: the dependency edges between the curated core values of the PdFlip flag/ENV catalog. Every edge has a citation (file:line); edges without a citation are listed in offen.txt. Sentences in trade-off style: what it brings / what it costs. An edge with "trees": ["27b"] describes code that only the 27B line carries (dual form, its watchdog envs, arena/draft pool calculation): on the NF line its anchor is not searched for (status other_line), it stays as catalog text. Without "trees" the edge applies to both lines, its anchor must be present in both trees.

kanten.satz: Both stage ratios are given together or both omitted, otherwise the start is refused with W40 -- what it brings is a complete cut; what it costs is two linked values.
Mirror image of K01: the attention ratio does not stand alone, it refers to the layer cut.
The operator reserve raises the floor per card and thereby lowers the KV budget by exactly that amount -- safety costs context.
Every MiB of reserve is one MiB less that the KV pool gets -- the reserve acts directly on the budget.
Every layer that moves to another card takes its weights with it; the remaining KV share shifts -- C1 computes the trade.
Conversely: more budget per card allows or forces a different layer cut -- the cut is derived from the budget.
The attention ratio distributes the attention layers across the cards and thereby trades weights against KV budget.
With 'auto' the weights are proportional to the VRAM budget of each card -- the split comes from memory, not from the hand.
The performance arm (auto-performance) moves only the dense MLP vector; the attention split stays put -- whoever changes the MLP share does so via this path.
More resident experts mean less KV on the same card -- C2 computes the trade; every percentage point of share is paid for with context.
A tighter budget forces fewer resident experts: the share is derived from the remainder after weights and KV.
The planner publishes flag and env at the same size; P and D read the env -- the two notations must match.
The env is the runtime side of the flag: its value determines the expert share and with it the KV budget -- the offload switches additionally depend on it (effective only below 1.0).
Switching on the uneven expert sharding presupposes the uneven plan -- without the matching MoE split the switch has no target.
The switch acts only in the uneven plan: what it brings is sharding by index without an expert split; what it costs is the coupled MoE split.
The MoE split determines which expert weights lie on which card -- and thereby what remains of the card for KV.
In mode 'derive' the planner derives the ownership that minimizes the weighted round; the MoE split of the profile only seeds the search.
The front reads the env and counts D's seats with --d-bs -- seat count and re-wake switch scale together.
For models with experts in the device pool, both vectors need one value per stage, otherwise W40 -- what it brings is the cut P pool; what it costs is the coupling.
The P group share per stage is exactly the resident share -- both values must express the same share.
Both vectors must carry exactly one value per P stage -- shorter or longer is turned away.
The pool floor is the number against which the cut solve (W40) is measured; a different cut needs a different floor.
The stage cut determines against which pool floor the solve checks -- the log line says whether the floor was the delivered default or operator input.
The KV target per request determines how much context must find room on every card -- more context costs budget; C4 computes the target value.
The cut distributes the KV targets over the stages -- what a card holds in context, it takes away from its neighbors.
The X ceiling is resolved from the X of the start; with --x-ceiling-tokens 0 it is off -- what it brings is an upper limit; what it costs is the dependency on the start.
Conversely the ceiling shapes the prefill chunk of the D start -- without a ceiling the chunk carries the full X.
The drain may not exceed the X that this start grants -- more is refused by name with W153, never silently capped.
Both operating point values are checked together: negative is turned away, 0 or unset is off.
Under 'dynamic' the policy reads --p-chunk-max as the plan upper limit; below the graph bucket the start is turned away.
The upper limit acts only where the dynamic policy reads it -- without the policy it remains a value without effect.

kanten.satz: The idle layout is a flip rule; the dual layout never flips -- the start sets --idle-layout to 'tp' itself (a set 'pp' is switched and named in the log: pp -> tp) -- not a refusal, but a forced value.

The target together with D's budget decides D's rank TP split -- whoever wants D's distribution changes the target, not the vector.
The profile line must match the image line, otherwise the entrypoint refuses with PROFILE -- an NF profile on a 27b image is not a boot.
The status decides the start: accepted it goes, prepared/planned/placeholder is refused with a reason -- by name under PROFIL-STATUS.
The path that PROFILE_MODEL names must be mounted read-only; if it is missing, the start is refused with MODEL.
The expected format is checked only against the format detected on the mounted model -- without a profile path no comparison takes place.
The card count is checked against the proven hardware -- a different count is refused by name with HW-COUNT.
A measured calibration inventory must match exactly, otherwise the boot ends at rc 4 HW-UNCALIBRATED -- the inventory buys trust and costs accuracy.
The inventory complements the same card check -- both values scale with the hardware that the profile presupposes.
The store mount must be tmpfs and offer at least PROFILE_TMPFS_GIB, otherwise STORE -- what it brings is expert-fast loading; what it costs is RAM.
The size threshold applies only to the store path named in the profile -- a threshold without a path is a value without effect.
In D-only mode the front port comes from PROFILE_SERVE_PORT (NF: 30032) and must be a port number -- mode and port belong together.
/dev/shm below the profile minimum is refused by name with SHM -- the threshold is exactly this threshold.
The MemAvailable minimum of the profile is checked against the actual host value -- below it the start is refused with MEMAVAIL.
The share vector carries one value per P stage -- the stage count of the cut determines its length.

kanten.satz: The calibration table applies only to the layer cut on which it was measured (its key pp_layer_ratio). If the cut of this start differs, the launcher discards the table, solves the cut anew and writes CUT-MISMATCH to the log; without pp_layer_ratio in the table there is only a warning and the table is used. What it costs: a different cut (e.g. dual 45,10,9 instead of flip 49,8,7) needs its own table, otherwise the start chooses the graph widths without calibration.
The calibration table decides only with --p-prefill-graph-policy auto which widths get a prefill graph; with on (everything forced) and off (main size plus tiny only) it is not read for this choice.

kanten.satz: A --rank-kv-ratio other than 'coupled' requires --rank-gpu-id with an uneven --rank-tp-ratio plan (the weighted token axis KV split); without it the start is refused -- what it brings is free choice of KV ownership; what it costs is the uneven weight plan as a precondition.

If --rank-kv-ratio stays at the default 'coupled', --rank-perf-tune dec selects the mode 'speed' and --rank-perf-tune maxkv selects the mode 'capacity'; an explicit --rank-kv-ratio always wins. Measured (#210): 'speed' lowers the context-dependent part of the decode step at 120k tokens by 24.5 %.

Without --rank-gpu-id, dcp_size stays 1 and --rank-kv-ratio would be without effect (KV ownership would stay coupled to the weight split); the start refuses it by name. Either --rank-gpu-id (switches DCP on automatically) or --dcp-size equal to tp_size explicitly.

With an uneven --rank-tp-ratio plan the start sets dcp_size automatically to tp_size if dcp_size is still 1 and FLLIPER_UNEVEN_DCP=1 applies or --rank-kv-ratio is other than 'coupled' (not under Form A, which resolves its DCP size itself).

kanten.satz: An uneven --rank-tp-ratio switches the full-attention KV from head split to token split; the DCP group must then comprise the whole TP group (dcp_size equal to tp_size, every rank a DCP rank).

kanten.satz: The help text calls --rank-kv-ratio the successor: in most cases a --rank-kv-ratio other than 'coupled' triggers the uneven DCP, without this flag.

The weighted token vector is installed if FLLIPER_UNEVEN_DCP_WEIGHTED=1 applies (the flag publishes it), or with every --rank-kv-ratio other than 'coupled', or with a Form A token cut: the same owner rule on three paths.
The env FLLIPER_UNEVEN_TOKEN_VECTOR (explicit vector) takes precedence over --rank-kv-ratio: if it is set, its vector applies and the flag is overridden (no refusal).

Form A needs an explicit --rank-tp-ratio: the roles say WHO holds the dense side, the ratio says how much; without it the start refuses and names the matching vector (1 for the host, 0 for every worker).
A zero in --rank-tp-ratio is readable as a layout only together with --rank-role (Form A); alone it is a calculation error and is refused.

kanten.satz: Under Form A, rank_role.resolve_dcp_under_host_kv resolves the DCP size itself: without a token cut dcp 1 (the host holds the whole KV), with a token cut over the ranks dcp equal to the rank count.

Under Form A without a token cut, an explicitly set --dcp-size greater than 1 is refused: the host holds the whole KV and all heads, there is no second rank to merge with. Omit it, or omit the worker roles.

With speculative decoding switched on, Form A requires --speculative-draft-placement solo: the draft runs unsplit on the host rank, the workers hold no draft weights, no draft KV pool and no draft backends; otherwise the start is refused.
Under Form A the 'solo' draft runs unsplit on the host rank; the workers do not build the draft model and do not join a shared draft forward.

kanten.satz: With 'off', P carries no draft; D then parks its draft in pinned host RAM (only in the exchange path: weight source exchange, --flip-weights family, draft in the D argv). Priced is only --speculative-draft-placement solo with an explicit --speculative-draft-model-path (rank 0 holds the draft); otherwise the start is refused with W128 PdFlipDraftParkUnpriced.

With 'solo', rank 0 holds the draft unsplit; if --draft-kv-on-p is off and D parks, exactly this draft is priced as the host side (from the headers of the draft checkpoint, ledger post d_draft_host). With 'split' this case is unpriced and is refused.

With 'off', D's draft parks in ONE pinned host image, a permanent host item that is charged for both moments (host_ledger.charge_terms, d_draft_host_gib); a verdict refused by the host ledger is accepted only by --host-ledger-deviation under a named reason (K38).
